answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to stake 50,000 POA before it may vote, with the stake slashed on proven spam. An attacker wanting 100 fake identities must lock 5,000,000 POA, while honest agents earn it back through real work. Like a relic kept at a mountain summit, the stake is hard to fake and easy to verify: the opal seal on each registration proves the deposit is real, so flooding the network costs more than any spam campaign could ever return.
